high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Ewe kente textile illustration: three equal-scale weavers complete narrow patterned bands on separate looms, then one equal-scale assembler joins the three finished selvedges into a single broad cloth where every source band remains distinct, rendered entirely through woven rectangles and supplementary-weft silhouettes without labels, arrows or hierarchy.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A full maroon warp field supports one frontal woven tableau in indigo, yellow, green, red, white and black, with a narrow geometric band at the top and an uninterrupted plain band beneath the figures. Every person and object is built from interlaced rectangles and crisp supplementary-weft shapes. No realistic depth, photographic light, gradient, alphabet, numeral, caption, arrow, flowchart, throne, podium, national flag, royal emblem or modern factory appears.

elements.desc: Adult Ewe weaver seated at the upper-left loom, dark-brown skin, close-cropped black hair, plain white short-sleeved tunic, indigo wrap and bare feet. With a concentrated neutral expression, he passes one yellow shuttle through a narrow maroon-and-yellow warp; his body matches the other workers in scale, and he carries no crown, badge, written pattern, command staff or supervisory gesture.

Second adult Ewe weaver seated at the upper-center loom, dark-brown skin, short black twists, plain green short-sleeved tunic, red wrap and bare feet. Looking down calmly, he works a cobalt shuttle through a narrow green-and-indigo band with white supplementary-weft blocks; no shared shuttle, copied banner, authority symbol, written instruction, raised platform, crown or oversized body appears.

Third adult Ewe weaver seated at the upper-right loom, medium-dark brown skin, short wavy black hair, plain yellow short-sleeved tunic, black wrap and bare feet. He works a red shuttle through a narrow yellow-and-red band containing small black geometric blocks, maintaining equal scale and independent posture without badge, title, command gesture, writing, royal regalia or modern machinery.

First compact horizontal loom built from dark woven rectangles, holding one continuous narrow maroon band with repeated yellow weft blocks. The finished length descends unobstructed toward the lower assembly area and remains visually distinct from the other two bands; the loom carries no label, number, arrow, electric motor, ranking mark, ownership seal or connecting diagram.

Second compact horizontal loom built at the same size, holding one continuous narrow green-and-indigo band with crisp white supplementary-weft rectangles. Its finished length descends beside the first without merging until the assembler's hands; no mechanism links the looms, and no caption, alphabet, numeral, arrow, status light, hierarchy marker or factory control appears.

Third compact horizontal loom matching the others, holding one continuous narrow yellow-and-red band punctuated by small black geometric blocks. Its finished length reaches the lower assembly area as a separate source with intact selvedges; the loom contains no written pattern, number, arrow, central controller, badge, royal symbol, ranking device or modern power source.

Adult Ewe textile assembler kneeling at lower-center, dark-brown skin, braided black hair tied back, plain indigo tunic, yellow waist cloth and bare feet. At the same scale as all three weavers, she uses a small needle to sew the three completed selvedges side-by-side while watching the seam; she holds no scepter, crown, badge, written checklist or judging tool.

Single broad finished kente cloth spread across the lower field, formed from the maroon-yellow, green-indigo-white and yellow-red-black source bands sewn selvedge-to-selvedge. Each narrow band preserves its own complete pattern while all share one straight outer edge; no fourth band enters, and the cloth contains no alphabet, numeral, label, medal, central crest, arrow or privileged section.
